clue.text: Manoeuvre van backwards to one entrance

indicators.note: backwards tells us the word van is to be read from its end to its start

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
a gate is a way in, an entrance

explanation.surface: A driver reverses a van so it lines up with a single doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backwards' turns VAN into NAV.
explanation.definitionFit: To steer or direct a course through somewhere is to manoeuvre.

clue.text: Drink of the Gods gets Cretan drunk

indicators.note: drunk suggests a reeling, confused state, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man from Crete gets intoxicated on divine liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges CRETAN; Crete fits the Greek myth picture.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth, the sweet liquid the Olympians consumed alongside ambrosia.

clue.text: Invent ale cocktail for a saint

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so these letters are blended into a new order

explanation.surface: Devise a beer-based mixed drink named after a holy figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cocktail' rearranges INVENTALE.
explanation.definitionFit: St Valentine, the martyr whose feast day on 14 February is for lovers.

clue.text: Normal way of doing things in surgery

parts.note: a practice is a customary way of doing things

explanation.surface: A standard procedure in an operating theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a 'surgery' is a family doctor's office, the GP practice, not an operation.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage a local doctor's clinic is called a surgery.

clue.text: Going up, editor and I notice some beef

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the letters are read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Rising in status, an editor and I spot some meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going up' reverses EDISPOT in this down clue. Topside is a British name for a lean cut of beef from the hindquarter.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut of meat from the outer thigh of the cow, used for roasting.

clue.text: Criticises roofing material

explanation.surface: A builder complains about the tiles on a roof.
explanation.definitionFit: To pan or attack harshly in a review; also the thin grey stone tiles laid on roofs.

clue.text: Behave without reserve and allow locks to drop

explanation.surface: Relaxing at a party and untying a ponytail.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for relaxing and enjoying oneself freely; literally, permitting tresses to fall loose.

clue.text: Half of them steal pound

indicators.note: half of takes the first two of the four letters of them

explanation.surface: Some of them take money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pound' looks like currency in a theft picture; it is the verb, to beat.
explanation.definitionFit: To beat or pulse heavily, as a heart or headache does.

clue.text: Teams surround most of army weaponry

indicators.note: surround says the letters for teams go round the other piece

parts.note: sides are teams in a match

indicators.note: most of means the word army loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Squads encircle the bulk of a military force with their guns.
explanation.definitionFit: Pistols or swords carried at the belt, small personal weapons.

clue.text: Is able to, on that ravine

parts.note: yon is an old word for that, as in yon hill

explanation.surface: Someone manages to reach that deep gorge.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep gorge cut by a river is a large ravine.

clue.text: Bottom of ridge on part of intestine

parts.note: a col is the low point or dip in a mountain ridge, a saddle between peaks

explanation.surface: A geography lesson about the base of a hillside and the gut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottom of ridge' is not a first-letter or last-letter pick; it is COL, the lowest pass along a ridge.
explanation.definitionFit: The large bowel, the main stretch of the lower gut, is a section of intestine.

clue.text: Drunk did decorating

explanation.surface: Someone got intoxicated while doing up a house.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for heavily intoxicated; also having coated walls with a smooth layer of lime or gypsum.

clue.text: Something unusual: boy Tim ran off

indicators.note: off suggests going wrong or awry, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A strange event: a lad named Tim bolted away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' signals the anagram of BOYTIMRAN.
explanation.definitionFit: An abnormality or freak, a thing deviating from the norm.

clue.text: Brought back first-class food from ancient Nile region

indicators.note: brought back says the letters for first-class and food are to be read in reverse

parts.note: A1 means first-class, written AI in crosswords
a bun is a small bread roll, a kind of food

explanation.surface: Excellent provisions were returned from an old Egyptian territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brought back' turns AIBUN round as a whole. AI stands for A1, top quality.
explanation.definitionFit: The historic land along the river south of Egypt, today parts of Sudan.

clue.text: Holiday, perhaps, that's after the invoice

indicators.note: after says the letters for that's come behind those for the invoice

parts.note: a bill is an invoice for payment

explanation.surface: Someone considers a trip away once the bill has been paid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holiday' is the jazz singer Billie Holiday, not a vacation; 'perhaps' marks her as one example of the first name.
explanation.definitionFit: The singer Billie Holiday is an example of someone with this first name.

clue.text: Tons drunk on unusual medicine

indicators.note: drunk suggests a tipsy stagger, so the letters of tons are jumbled

parts.note: rum is an old British word for odd or unusual

explanation.surface: Getting heavily intoxicated on some strange remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' gives NOST from TONS; RUM in British slang means strange.
explanation.definitionFit: A quack remedy or pet cure, a patent medicine of doubtful worth.

clue.text: Listens during actual run-through

indicators.note: during means one piece occurs within the span of the other

explanation.surface: Someone pays attention throughout the genuine performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'actual' sounds like the definition of a rehearsal's opposite; it only supplies REAL, which 'during' splits.
explanation.definitionFit: A practice performance before the real show.

clue.text: It distributes using Spanish book enthusiast

parts.note: SP is the abbreviation for Spanish
a reader is a person keen on books

explanation.surface: A Spanish bibliophile hands things out.
explanation.definitionFit: A device or tool that scatters seed, fertiliser or butter is a spreader.

clue.text: Entertainer on quay is rubbish

parts.note: a pier is a landing stage, like a quay

explanation.surface: A seaside performer on the jetty is dismissed as hopeless.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantomime clown in a white costume, a stock stage performer.

clue.text: Hint, plea almost, for drink

indicators.note: almost means the word plea loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A suggestion, nearly a request, to have a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims PLEA to PLE.
explanation.definitionFit: An alcoholic beverage, especially one sipped habitually.

clue.text: Pressure on each year? Excellent!

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Asking whether annual pressure is a fine thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for splendid or wonderful, used as an exclamation.

clue.text: Personal assistant for every queen's decorator

parts.note: per means for each or for every
ER (Elizabeth Regina) is the crossword abbreviation for the Queen

explanation.surface: A secretary working for each royal's interior designer.
explanation.walkthrough: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who hangs wallpaper, a type of decorator.

clue.text: Slid over surface but takes wrong day

indicators.note: wrong suggests the letters are out of order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone glided across the ice but picked the wrong date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges TAKES to SKATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To glide across ice on blades is to have slid over a surface.

clue.text: The wrong one caught in a moral principle

indicators.note: wrong suggests the letters are out of order and must be rearranged

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A guilty party is detained, ensnared in a question of ethics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' gives ETH from THE; 'caught' is C in cricket scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: A rule of conduct or set of values guiding right behaviour.

clue.text: Well-built dog

explanation.surface: A strong, sturdy hound.
explanation.definitionFit: Big and strong in build; also an Arctic sled dog.

clue.text: FT support for this book

parts.note: the Financial Times is a newspaper, a paper

explanation.surface: The Financial Times endorses this volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'FT' is the Financial Times, the newspaper in which the puzzle appears.
explanation.definitionFit: A softcover edition, an inexpensive type of book.

clue.text: Sid backed cultivator, a whisky producer

indicators.note: backed tells us the name Sid is read from its end

parts.note: a tiller is a machine or person that tills the soil

explanation.surface: Sid put money on a farmer who also makes spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns SID into DIS; it looks like betting support.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm or person who makes spirits by evaporating and condensing alcohol.

clue.text: Beginning where film star works

explanation.surface: Opening day at the studio for a screen actor.
explanation.definitionFit: The start of something; also on the movie stage, where acting takes place.

clue.text: Hers and my assorted poems

indicators.note: assorted means mixed up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A couple's verses gathered together in one collection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assorted' rearranges HERSMY.
explanation.definitionFit: Verses with matching sounds at line ends stand for poetry generally.

clue.text: Skin inside was bleeding in brown streaks

indicators.note: inside says one piece sits within the other

parts.note: bled means was bleeding, lost blood
rind is the tough outer skin of fruit or cheese

explanation.surface: A wounded animal's hide is marked with streaks of brown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'was bleeding' reads as a description of the skin, but it is just the past tense, holding the skin word.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes a coat, such as a cow's or dog's, tawny with darker flecks or bands.
